title: Pulse-driven Priority Allocator for Tiered Quota Admission
creator: Asha Nambiar
description: Implement a pulse-driven priority allocator that makes admission and demotion decisions for free/paid/enterprise lanes based on short periodic snapshots (pulses) of quota states, latency headroom, and regional capacity. The allocator should: 1) compute per-tenant priority scores combining plan tier, recent consumption velocity, token-bucket credits, and SLA tier; 2) emit admission hints to the request router (allow/throttle/downgrade) per pulse window; 3) coordinate graceful fallback to cheaper model variants and regional spillover when capacity or quota pressure is detected; 4) preserve low-latency fast-path for enterprise SLO-bound traffic while smoothing bursts from free tier users.
design_notes: Core idea: replace strictly reactive single-request checks with a lightweight periodic eval (default pulse=1s) that updates in-memory tenant priority vectors. Implementation will use an append-only ring buffer for recent consumption rates, a small ranked skiplist per region to surface high-priority tenants, and a compact admission bitmap broadcast to edge routers. We'll also expose a feature flag to toggle 'pulse mode' and an instrumentation endpoint for inspecting the current pulse state.
algorithm_summary: 1) On pulse tick, read quota reports and per-tenant token bucket; 2) compute score = alpha*(tier_weight) + beta*(remaining_credits/expected_hourly_usage) - gamma*(latency_debt) + delta*(regional_affinity_bonus); 3) rank tenants, assign admission buckets [Guaranteed, BestEffort, DemoteCandidate]; 4) publish admission decisions to local router cache; 5) DemoteCandidate requests are tagged and redirected to fallback model variant or queued with soft-defer.
api_contract: Routing service changes: new /v1/admision/pulse-status (read) and /v1/tenant/{id}/priority (read). Router accepts admission hints in request headers: X-Redwood-Admission: Guaranteed|BestEffort|Demote. Fallback model variants defined per tenant in tenant-config with keys: fallback_model_id and max_demote_rate.
acceptance_criteria: Pulse mode can be enabled via a feature flag without downtime
Under synthetic burst tests, free-tier 95th percentile latency increases by <10% while paid-tier p99 remains within SLO
Fallback model redirection preserves success rate for demo workloads and reduces host GPU token load by >=20% during sustained bursts
Admission hints are emitted at <=1s latency after pulse evaluation and consumed by edge routers
Unit + integration tests covering priority scoring, region spill, and model fallback are present and green
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy pulse evaluator with feature flag; run chaos/synthetic bursts using kafka-replay against staging cluster
Phase 2 (canary): enable for internal tenants only (tenant whitelist), monitor p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token, and error-rate for 48h
Phase 3 (region-limited): enable in us-west-2 for subset of public tenants; add automated rollback triggers if p99 > SLO or model-fallback rate > 15%
Phase 4 (global): gradual enable with ramping factor and adjustments to alpha/beta weights based on observed telemetry

metrics_and_monitoring: Model variant traffic fraction and fallback rate
p50/p95/p99 latency by tier and by admission bucket
Pulse evaluator CPU and memory (should be <5% of control-plane budget)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: oscillation when pulse window too short -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum sticky duration for demotion
Risk: incorrect tenant scoring due to stale metrics -> Mitigation: fallback to request-level token-bucket checks if pulse data is older than threshold
Risk: overload in pulse evaluator under millions of tenants -> Mitigation: shard evaluator by region and sample low-activity tenants
Risk: security/abuse via spoofed admission headers -> Mitigation: routers must validate hints against signed admission token published by control-plane
